newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high, electronics fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high, electronics fall.

text.p: Taiwan's stock market celebrated the constitutional assembly's adoption of key political reforms, pushing to a higher close on Monday despite heavy profit-taking on electronics, brokers said.
The index surged to a seven-year intraday high 9,896.73 but saw profit-takers erode the gains in late trade to finish at 9,833.77 points, up 84.47 points or 0.87 percent.
The index had not closed higher since finishing at 9,978.86 on April 12, 1990.
Turnover was extremely heavy at T$231.8 billion.
The recently uninspired financial sector, led by the "big three" state-run banks, surged 5.28 percent to leave electronics in its wake as the session's trendsetting sector, brokers said.
The big three -- Chang Hwa Bank, First Commercial Bank and Hua Nan Bank -- all rose the daily seven percent limit to T$133, T$134.5 and T$135, respectively.
All are seen benefitting from Taiwan's political reforms.

"This was a celebration rally after completion (on Friday) of the constitutional reforms," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien. "As electronics plunged, investors switched their buying to financials to keep the bullish uptrend."
Brokers said the buying focus had turned to financials as the sector had been consolidating in recent weeks during a dazzling bull run by electronics that has led the overall index sharply higher.

Brokers said they expected the big three banks' planned privatisation to accelerate now that the constitutional assembly has completed amendments that will all but phase out their principal owner -- the Taiwan provincial government.
In late May, the government announced a 12-18 month plan to release 15.9 percent of First Commercial's shares, 7.5 percent of Hua Nan's and 4.65 percent of Chang Hwa's.
